summary: Independent GRAVEYARD red-team pass challenged the exact 12-company batch. No bearish conclusion was forced. The highest-priority hidden-risk clusters are NBIS financing/capital intensity, IONQ acquisition integration and cash consumption, BTDR tenant/backstop/buildout dependence, OKLO licensing-versus-commercialization gap, and concentration/architecture risks across CRDO/ALAB/SYM/NVDA/AMD. GEV remains the only batch name with a publishable canonical record; all others retain unresolved thesis-breaker gaps.

materialFindings.finding: Large contracted AI demand does not remove financing risk. A $775M secured facility backed by GPU assets/contracted cash flows demonstrates financeability but also makes asset utilization, counterparty performance and refinancing structure first-order risk variables; the separate $5B convertible financing flagged by underwriting increases dilution/capital-structure complexity.

Vertical integration can accelerate engineering while simultaneously magnifying integration/capital risk. SkyWater consideration included cash and stock, while the acquired foundry must continue serving third parties; execution therefore depends on integrating a different operating model without degrading merchant-customer economics.

The $4.7B AI/HPC lease is not equivalent to guaranteed realized revenue. Tenant obligations are described as anticipated to receive roughly $1.3B of letters-of-credit support subject to conditions, and Bitdeer must deliver 121 IT MW. Construction, financing, tenant credit and power-delivery execution remain material falsification paths.

Atomic Alchemy's NRC materials license is a real regulatory milestone but cannot be used as evidence that Oklo's Aurora reactor licensing/commercial schedule is de-risked. Treating a subsidiary isotope license as reactor-license progress would be a category error.

evidence: Current SEC stream contains multiple insider Form 4/144 filings and an EFFECT filing.
contradictions: Strong space-systems optionality coexists with launch-development capital intensity.
unknowns: Neutron schedule/cost-to-complete, backlog margin quality, insider-sale context
falsifiers: Repeated Neutron slips plus rising external financing need; backlog growth without cash conversion.

evidence: Fresh 10-Q/S-8 and results 8-K are available; optical acquisition strategy expands TAM.
contradictions: Very rapid growth can mask hyperscaler concentration and cycle dependence.
unknowns: Top-customer concentration, stock-comp dilution, DustPhotonics integration
falsifiers: Meaningful socket loss at a top customer or gross-margin compression that persists through optical ramp.

evidence: Q2 growth and Scorpio ramp are company-verified.
contradictions: Product-family expansion increases opportunity but does not prove resilience against hyperscaler custom silicon or standardization.
unknowns: Customer concentration, platform dependence, stock-comp dilution
falsifiers: Scorpio fails to broaden customers or price/margin erosion follows open-standard competition.

evidence: Backlog/order acceleration is strong and canonical evidence is mature.
contradictions: Long-cycle backlog can still hide execution, working-capital and supply-chain risk.
unknowns: Order cancellation/deferral sensitivity, transformer/core-steel constraint duration
falsifiers: Backlog-to-revenue conversion weakens materially or electrification margins fail to improve despite scale.

evidence: Large commitments and secured financing are real.
contradictions: Scale is being purchased through extraordinary capex/financing; customer concentration can turn contractual strength into counterparty dependency.
unknowns: Post-convert dilution, project IRRs, Meta/Microsoft concentration
falsifiers: Utilization/pricing below underwritten levels, customer delays, or repeated equity/convert issuance to bridge capex.

evidence: Fresh 10-Q exists and sovereign-launch partnership adds optionality.
contradictions: Strategic relevance of daily imagery does not guarantee attractive unit economics after constellation replacement capex.
unknowns: Government concentration, renewal quality, satellite replacement cash burden
falsifiers: Backlog/revenue growth without operating leverage or replacement capex persistently consumes free cash flow.

contradictions: Regulatory progress in isotope handling is not reactor commercialization.
unknowns: Aurora application milestones, first-site capex, fuel availability, financing
falsifiers: Reactor licensing timeline materially slips or project financing requires sustained dilution at uneconomic terms.

evidence: 121 IT MW lease and Texas expansion verified.
contradictions: Contract headline value precedes construction completion and depends on tenant/backstop conditions.
unknowns: Fully funded capex, final LC terms, delivery penalties, mining-to-AI transition costs
falsifiers: Backstop conditions fail, energization slips, or capital cost materially exceeds lease economics.

evidence: SkyWater close and Superion prototype milestones verified.
contradictions: Roadmap acceleration is management-reported while profitability and integration economics remain unresolved.
unknowns: Post-close liquidity, purchase accounting, merchant-foundry conflicts, true quantum-compute demand
falsifiers: Superion delivery slips, SkyWater third-party business deteriorates, or cash burn accelerates without corresponding commercial adoption.

contradictions: Automation backlog narratives can overstate economics when deployments are customer-concentrated and implementation-heavy.
unknowns: Top-customer dependence, deployment margin, accounting-control durability
falsifiers: Large-customer delays/cancellations or margin deterioration as backlog converts.

contradictions: Dominant demand can coexist with customer concentration, export-control loss of reachable market and hyperscaler internal-silicon substitution.
unknowns: Export-control sensitivity, customer concentration, inventory/capex digestion
falsifiers: Cloud capex slows while accelerator supply catches demand; export restrictions expand; internal accelerators materially displace merchant GPUs.

contradictions: AI accelerator TAM growth does not guarantee share capture against entrenched CUDA ecosystem and custom silicon.
unknowns: MI-series customer breadth, ROCm switching costs, export exposure
falsifiers: Major customers fail to expand deployments after pilots or software ecosystem gaps persist despite hardware competitiveness.

proposedCanonicalChanges.proposal: Before any score advancement, require explicit capital-structure/integration stress cases for NBIS, IONQ and BTDR and a reactor-specific licensing bridge for OKLO.

contradictions.issue: Several batch companies have strong headline growth/contract/product signals while the financial evidence needed to determine capital efficiency and dilution remains incomplete; headline scale must not substitute for underwriting.

unknowns.unknown: Full fresh filing extraction is incomplete for RKLB, CRDO, SYM, NVDA and AMD, limiting accounting-quality and concentration tests.

peerRequests.request: Extract concentration, liquidity, dilution and project/acquisition economics for NBIS, IONQ, BTDR, OKLO, CRDO and ALAB before rubric completion.

accuracyDebates.topic: Should large announced contract values be treated as realized economic proof?
accuracyDebates.position: No. Contract tenor, termination rights, customer/backstop credit, delivery obligations, capex and margin determine realized economics.

blockingIssues.issue: Eleven batch names remain methodology-incomplete and several material risk dimensions require deeper primary-field extraction; red-team acquisition is therefore not complete.

directivesReviewed.result: XTND is outside the provisional 12-company batch; preserved as an open blocker and not conflated with batch work.
